comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C30, C36, C37, C43. Both evaluations find the tonotopic pattern and frequency-dependent effects well-supported by experimental data with appropriate statistical tests. Reviewers explicitly affirm 'compelling evidence' for the core finding.

Perfect agreement on claims C31, C38, C39, C44, C57. Both evaluations support the salicylate control experiments demonstrating OHC involvement. OpenEval notes incomplete inhibition variability while peer reviewers find the control 'corroborates' OHC involvement without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C32, C40, C41, C42, C45. Both evaluations affirm frequency-specific effects with tones being more effective than noise. Peer reviewers find this 'especially interesting' due to traveling-wave phase profiles.

Strong agreement on computational modeling claims C33, C34, C68-C72. Both find the modeling work supports the proposed mechanism. OpenEval notes model simplifications requiring justification while peer reviewers describe the modeling as 'elegant' without raising concerns about limitations.

Perfect agreement on claim C35. Both evaluations support the tonotopic pattern of drug delivery. OpenEval explicitly references Figure 1G while peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of overall experimental results.

Both address claims C46, C47, C54 about OHC-driven fluid circulation as a novel finding. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes these are interpretive claims about broader significance. Peer reviewers unanimously recognize this as a major contribution and 'first report to test the pumping effect in vivo.'

Perfect agreement on claim C56. Both evaluations support the finding that facilitation extends beyond CF location. Peer reviewers find the spatial pattern 'especially interesting' and accept it as part of the validated mechanism.

Divergent evaluations on speculative claims C63, C64, C73. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable extrapolations lacking direct experimental support. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as reasonable implications and logical extensions, with one noting 'thoughtfully discussed' future applications.

Both address claim C73 about drug delivery applications. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental support. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating it as a reasonable future application and logical extension of findings.

Strong agreement on background claims C1-C18 (OpenEval) overlapping with C1-C20 (peer review). Both evaluations support these as established context with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm clinical motivation regarding lack of noninvasive drug delivery methods.

Strong agreement on prior work claims C19-C26. Both evaluations support these as established background and appropriate characterization of the knowledge gap. Peer reviewers emphasize this is 'the first report to test the pumping effect in vivo.'

Perfect agreement on claim C27 (central hypothesis). Both evaluations support that the hypothesis was well-motivated and successfully tested. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'the authors successfully validated their hypothesis.'

Perfect agreement on claims C28, C29 regarding kainic acid methodology. Both evaluations support this methodological choice with appropriate justification. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by noting 'well-established electrophysiological method.'

Perfect agreement on claims C48-C53 about current knowledge and controversy. Both evaluations support these as accurate representation of the field with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accept the discussion about OHC function beyond traditional amplification models.

Divergent evaluations on evolutionary/speculative claims C59-C62. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting evolutionary reasoning is plausible but lacks direct experimental support. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as reasonable implications for cochlear homeostasis.

Perfect agreement on claims C65-C67 about relationship to prior work. Both evaluations support these as accurate characterization with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as established context for cochlear fluid dynamics.

Perfect agreement on methodological claims C74-C77. Both evaluations affirm the experimental and computational methods are sound with adequate sample sizes. Peer reviewers praise the 'synergistic use' of electrophysiology and computational modeling.
